content.text:
Now I have a complete picture. Let me provide a comprehensive analysis of the visual issues.

---

## Landing Page Visual Issues Analysis

### 1. Navigation Component (`/apps/web/src/components/landing/navigation.tsx`)

**Current Styling:**
- **Background:** `bg-foreground` with `backdrop-blur-md` and `border-background/10`
- **Text colors:** `text-background`, `text-background/60`
- **Primary button:** Uses `bg-gradient-to-r from-primary to-primary` with `text-white`

**Analysis:** 
This is an **intentional dark section** using the inverted pattern (`bg-foreground` + `text-background`). This should work correctly in both light and dark mode because:
- In light mode: foreground is dark, background is light
- In dark mode: foreground is light, background is dark

**Status:** No contrast issues - correctly implements inverted color scheme.

---

### 2. Hero Section (`/apps/web/src/components/landing/hero-section.tsx`)

**Current Styling:**
- **Background:** Uses `mesh-gradient` class
- **Text colors:** `text-foreground`, `text-muted-foreground` for description
- **Badge:** `bg-card/50`, `border-border`, `text-muted-foreground`
- **Input:** `bg-card/80`, `border-border`, `text-foreground`, placeholder `text-muted-foreground`
- **Primary button:** Uses `bg-gradient-to-r from-primary to-primary` with `text-white`

**Mesh Gradient Definition (from `/apps/web/src/index.css`):**
```css
.mesh-gradient {
  background-color: #ffffff;  /* HARDCODED WHITE */
  background-image:
    radial-gradient(at 0% 0%, hsl(var(--primary) / 0.05) 0, transparent 50%),
    ...
}
```

**ISSUE IDENTIFIED:**
- **`background-color: #ffffff`** is hardcoded white! This does NOT adapt to dark mode.
- In dark mode, the hero will have a white background which looks wrong.
- Should use `hsl(var(--background))` or `bg-background` class instead.

**Status:** HAS DARK MODE ISSUE - hardcoded white background in mesh-gradient.

---

### 3. Social Proof Section (`/apps/web/src/components/landing/social-proof.tsx`)

**Current Styling:**
- **Background:** None specified (transparent/inherits from parent)
- **Text colors:** `text-muted-foreground` for "Trusted by product teams at"
- **Logos:** Using CSS mask technique with `backgroundColor: "hsl(var(--foreground))"`

**Logo Implementation:**
```tsx
<div
  className="mask-image h-8 w-24 bg-foreground"
  style={{
    backgroundColor: "hsl(var(--foreground))",
  }}
/>
```

**Analysis:**
- The logos use the CSS mask technique with foreground color
- In light mode: foreground is dark, so logos appear dark
- In dark mode: foreground is light, so logos appear light

**ISSUE IDENTIFIED:**
- The company logos use SVGs with hardcoded `stroke="black"` and `fill="black"` in the base64-encoded content
- When the mask applies foreground color, in dark mode the logos become light/white
- However, the section background is not explicitly dark, so light logos on a potentially light background may have poor visibility
- The parent section styling matters here - if it's on a light background in dark mode, the light logos won't show well

**Status:** POTENTIAL ISSUE - logos may not be visible in dark mode if parent section has light background. Need to ensure social proof is on a dark section OR the logos have proper contrast handling.

---

# Landing Page Dark Mode Contrast Fixes ## Context After the theme refactoring, several landing page components have visual issues in dark mode due to: 1. Hardcoded background colors that don't adapt to theme 2. Inverted color scheme applied incorrectly (light backgrounds in dark mode) 3. Logo elements with poor contrast against their backgrounds **User-reported issues:** - Dark mode top header has bright background with muted/grayish text (poor contrast) - Hero section in dark mode has bright background but uses light text (poor readability) - "Trusted by product teams at" logos are not visible (black on black basically) - Footer should have coloring similar to "Loved by teams worldwide" section --- ## Root Cause Analysis ### Issue 1: Hero Section - Hardcoded White Background **File:** `apps/web/src/index.css` (line 110) The `.mesh-gradient` class has a hardcoded white background: ```css .mesh-gradient { background-color: #ffffff; /* HARDCODED - doesn't adapt to dark mode */ ... } ``` **Problem:** In dark mode, hero section stays white while text uses `text-foreground` (which becomes light), resulting in light text on white background - unreadable. ### Issue 2: Navigation - Inverted Color Scheme in Dark Mode **File:** `apps/web/src/components/landing/navigation.tsx` The navigation uses `bg-foreground` with `text-background` (inverted scheme): - Light mode: dark nav bar with light text ✓ - Dark mode: light nav bar with dark text ✗ (user expects dark nav bar) **Problem:** The inverted scheme flips in dark mode, making the navigation bright when users expect it to remain dark for visual consistency. **Solution:** Navigation should always be dark - use explicit dark colors instead of theme variables. ### Issue 3: Social Proof - Invisible Logos in Dark Mode **File:** `apps/web/src/components/landing/social-proof.tsx` Logos use `bg-foreground` with CSS mask technique: - Light mode: foreground is dark → dark logos on light background ✓ - Dark mode: foreground is light → light logos on light background (from hero) ✗ **Problem:** Social proof sits after hero section. In dark mode: - Hero has white background (hardcoded) - Logos become light (foreground is light in dark mode) - Result: invisible light-on-light ### Issue 4: Footer - Different Style Than Testimonials **File:** `apps/web/src/components/landing/footer/index.tsx` Footer uses `bg-foreground` (inverted, always dark in light mode, always light in dark mode). Testimonials uses `bg-muted` (adapts to theme, light gray in light mode, dark gray in dark mode). **Problem:** Footer should use a consistent "dark section" approach that works in both modes. --- ## Implementation Plan ### Fix 1: Mesh Gradient - Use Theme Variable **File:** `apps/web/src/index.css` ```diff .mesh-gradient { - background-color: #ffffff; + background-color: hsl(var(--background)); background-image: radial-gradient(at 0% 0%, hsl(var(--primary) / 0.05) 0, transparent 50%), ... } ``` This makes the hero background adapt to theme: light in light mode, dark in dark mode. ### Fix 2: Navigation - Force Dark Styling **File:** `apps/web/src/components/landing/navigation.tsx` Replace theme-based colors with explicit dark colors that work in both modes: ```diff -
